classification.difficultyReason: Express two fruit masses using expenditure and unit price, solve the resulting fractional equation, and interpret both masses.

content.prompt: David buys $\$2x$ worth of grapes at $\$5$ a kilogram, and $\$x$ worth of peaches at $\$7$ a kilogram. He buys a total of 10 kg of peaches and grapes. How much of each fruit does he buy?

answer.short:
Grapes: $7\frac{7}{19}\text{ kg}$. Peaches: $2\frac{12}{19}\text{ kg}$.

Divide each expenditure by its price per kilogram, then use the total mass to form an equation.
answer.worked:
Mass equals expenditure divided by price per kilogram. The grapes have mass $\frac{2x}{5}$ kg and the peaches have mass $\frac{x}{7}$ kg.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2x}{5}+\frac{x}{7}&=10\\14x+5x&=350\\19x&=350\\x&=\frac{350}{19}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Mass of grapes}&=\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{350}{19}\\\text{Mass of grapes}&=\frac{140}{19}\text{ kg}\\\text{Mass of grapes}&=7\frac{7}{19}\text{ kg}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Mass of peaches}&=\frac{1}{7}\times\frac{350}{19}\\\text{Mass of peaches}&=\frac{50}{19}\text{ kg}\\\text{Mass of peaches}&=2\frac{12}{19}\text{ kg}\end{align*}$$
Check: $\frac{140}{19}+\frac{50}{19}=10$ kg.
